input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# disk_monitor_cleanup.sh — Monitor disk usage on multiple remote servers
# via SSH and clean up old files when usage exceeds a threshold.
#
# Usage:
#   ./disk_monitor_cleanup.sh [-c config_file] [-t threshold] [-d max_age_days] [-p path] [-n dry_run]
#
# Options:
#   -c  Config file with one host per line (default: ./servers.conf)
#   -t  Disk usage threshold percentage to trigger cleanup (default: 80)
#   -d  Delete files older than this many days (default: 30)
#   -p  Remote path to clean up (default: /tmp)
#   -n  Dry run — show what would be deleted without deleting
#   -h  Show help
#
# Config file format (one per line):
#   user@host
#   user@host:port
#   # comments and blank lines are ignored

set -euo pipefail

# ── Defaults ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CONFIG_FILE="./servers.conf"
THRESHOLD=80
MAX_AGE_DAYS=30
CLEANUP_PATH="/tmp"
DRY_RUN=false
SSH_OPTS="-o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new"

# ── Colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m'

# ── Functions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
    sed -n '2,/^$/s/^# \?//p' "$0"
    exit 0
}

log_info()  { printf "${CYAN}[INFO]${NC}  %s\n" "$*"; }
log_ok()    { printf "${GREEN}[OK]${NC}    %s\n" "$*"; }
log_warn()  { printf "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC}  %s\n" "$*"; }
log_err()   { printf "${RED}[ERR]${NC}   %s\n" "$*"; }

parse_host() {
    # Split user@host:port into HOST and PORT
    local entry="$1"
    local host port
    if [[ "$entry" == *:* ]]; then
        host="${entry%%:*}"
        port="${entry##*:}"
    else
        host="$entry"
        port="22"
    fi
    HOST="$host"
    PORT="$port"
}

check_and_cleanup() {
    local entry="$1"
    parse_host "$entry"

    log_info "Connecting to ${HOST} (port ${PORT}) ..."

    # Get disk usage percentage for the partition containing CLEANUP_PATH
    local usage
    usage=$(ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" \
        "df -P '${CLEANUP_PATH}' 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2 {gsub(/%/,\"\"); print \$5}'" 2>/dev/null) || {
        log_err "Failed to connect to ${HOST}:${PORT}"
        return 1
    }

    if [[ -z "$usage" || ! "$usage" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        log_err "Could not read disk usage from ${HOST}:${PORT}"
        return 1
    fi

    if (( usage < THRESHOLD )); then
        log_ok "${HOST}:${PORT} — ${CLEANUP_PATH} usage is ${usage}% (threshold ${THRESHOLD}%) — no action needed"
        return 0
    fi

    log_warn "${HOST}:${PORT} — ${CLEANUP_PATH} usage is ${usage}% (threshold ${THRESHOLD}%) — cleaning up files older than ${MAX_AGE_DAYS} days"

    # Find old files and report sizes
    local find_cmd="find '${CLEANUP_PATH}' -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +${MAX_AGE_DAYS} -ls 2>/dev/null"
    local count
    count=$(ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" "$find_cmd | wc -l" 2>/dev/null) || count=0

    if (( count == 0 )); then
        log_warn "${HOST}:${PORT} — No files older than ${MAX_AGE_DAYS} days found in ${CLEANUP_PATH}"
        return 0
    fi

    local total_size
    total_size=$(ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" \
        "find '${CLEANUP_PATH}' -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +${MAX_AGE_DAYS} -printf '%s\n' 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=\$1} END {printf \"%.1f MB\", s/1048576}'" 2>/dev/null) || total_size="unknown"

    log_info "${HOST}:${PORT} — Found ${count} file(s) totaling ${total_size}"

    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
        log_info "${HOST}:${PORT} — [DRY RUN] Would delete:"
        ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" \
            "find '${CLEANUP_PATH}' -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +${MAX_AGE_DAYS} -printf '  %t  %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" \
            "find '${CLEANUP_PATH}' -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +${MAX_AGE_DAYS} -delete" 2>/dev/null || {
            log_err "${HOST}:${PORT} — Cleanup failed"
            return 1
        }

        # Report new usage
        local new_usage
        new_usage=$(ssh -p "$PORT" $SSH_OPTS "$HOST" \
            "df -P '${CLEANUP_PATH}' 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2 {gsub(/%/,\"\"); print \$5}'" 2>/dev/null) || new_usage="?"
        log_ok "${HOST}:${PORT} — Cleaned up ${count} file(s). Usage now: ${new_usage}%"
    fi
}

# ── Parse arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
while getopts "c:t:d:p:nh" opt; do
    case "$opt" in
        c) CONFIG_FILE="$OPTARG" ;;
        t) THRESHOLD="$OPTARG" ;;
        d) MAX_AGE_DAYS="$OPTARG" ;;
        p) CLEANUP_PATH="$OPTARG" ;;
        n) DRY_RUN=true ;;
        h) usage ;;
        *) usage ;;
    esac
done

# ── Validate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    log_err "Config file not found: $CONFIG_FILE"
    log_info "Create a servers.conf with one 'user@host' per line."
    exit 1
fi

if ! [[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( THRESHOLD < 1 || THRESHOLD > 100 )); then
    log_err "Threshold must be an integer between 1 and 100"
    exit 1
fi

if ! [[ "$MAX_AGE_DAYS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( MAX_AGE_DAYS < 1 )); then
    log_err "Max age days must be a positive integer"
    exit 1
fi

# ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
printf "\n${CYAN}━━━ Disk Monitor & Cleanup ━━━${NC}\n"
printf "  Config:    %s\n" "$CONFIG_FILE"
printf "  Threshold: %s%%\n" "$THRESHOLD"
printf "  Max age:   %s days\n" "$MAX_AGE_DAYS"
printf "  Path:      %s\n" "$CLEANUP_PATH"
printf "  Dry run:   %s\n\n" "$DRY_RUN"

failures=0
total=0

while IFS= read -r line; do
    # Skip blank lines and comments
    line="${line%%#*}"
    line="${line// /}"
    [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

    (( total++ )) || true
    check_and_cleanup "$line" || (( failures++ )) || true
    echo
done < "$CONFIG_FILE"

printf "${CYAN}━━━ Done: %d server(s) processed, %d failure(s) ━━━${NC}\n" "$total" "$failures"
exit "$failures"

content.text:
Created two files:

**`disk_monitor_cleanup.sh`** — the main script. It:

1. Reads a list of servers from a config file (default `./servers.conf`)
2. SSHs into each server and checks disk usage on a target path
3. If usage exceeds the threshold, finds and deletes files older than N days
4. Reports before/after usage for each server

**Usage examples:**

```bash
# Basic run with defaults (80% threshold, clean /tmp files older than 30 days)
./disk_monitor_cleanup.sh

# Dry run — see what would be deleted without deleting
./disk_monitor_cleanup.sh -n

# Custom threshold, age, path, and config file
./disk_monitor_cleanup.sh -c prod_servers.conf -t 90 -d 14 -p /var/log

# Custom SSH port is set per-host in the config file
# e.g. admin@db-server:2222
```

**Config file format** (`servers.conf`):
```
user@host
user@host:port
# comments and blank lines are ignored
```

**Options:**

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `-c` | `./servers.conf` | Config file path |
| `-t` | `80` | Usage % threshold to trigger cleanup |
| `-d` | `30` | Delete files older than N days |
| `-p` | `/tmp` | Remote path to monitor/clean |
| `-n` | off | Dry run (list files, don't delete) |

The script uses `df -P` for portable disk usage parsing, limits `find` to `-maxdepth 1` to avoid recursive deletion, and exits with the number of failures as the exit code.
